overview.summary: Toki is an internal team chat for one company: channels, direct messages, threads and files, and later tasks, calendar, video meetings, a guest portal, automations, mail and AI summaries. Each company runs its own copy on its own server.
product: A real product, built in phases
Internal use first, up to about 200 people
The prototype is the only design source
Phase 1 is core chat on the web
technical: Server: Node and TypeScript, modular monolith
Sign-in with a 6-digit code sent by email
status: Phase 1 requirements are closed: every brainstorming question, review question and assumption is decided.
The intent list (17) and the ticket list are drafts awaiting review. No ticket exists on GitHub yet.
No `intent.md` or `spec.md` has been written. Nothing has been committed to the repository.
Six items are deliberately left open; none blocks phase 1. They are listed under Questions & Gaps.

decisions.q: What do you want to build from this prototype: a real product that runs in production, a front end on mock data for demos, or a heavily cut first version?
decisions.a: (a) A real product, built in phases
decisions.options: (a) Real product · (b) Front end on mock data · (c) Heavily cut MVP

decisions.q: The prototype holds 14 feature groups. Which of them must be in the first release?
decisions.a: Core chat, Activity, Later, Files, People, Preferences, command palette
decisions.options: Pick from the prototype's 14 feature groups

decisions.q: The prototype shows a Desktop app, Web and Phone. Which platforms does the first release need?
decisions.a: (a) Responsive web first
decisions.options: (a) Responsive web · (b) Web + desktop · (c) Web + desktop + mobile

decisions.q: Does one installation of Toki serve one company on its own server, or does one system serve many companies like Slack?
decisions.a: (a), keeping workspace_id in the schema
decisions.options: (a) Single-tenant self-hosted · (b) Multi-tenant SaaS

decisions.q: Do you or your team have any technology constraints: language, framework, database, cloud?
decisions.a: TypeScript, React, Postgres, WebSocket
decisions.options: Any constraints

decisions.q: Real video calling is the heaviest subsystem in the prototype. Self-host an open-source media server, use a hosted service, only link out to Google Meet or Zoom, or drop it from the roadmap?
decisions.a: (a) Self-hosted LiveKit, in its own phase
decisions.options: (a) Self-hosted SFU · (b) Hosted service · (c) Link out to Google Meet · (d) Drop

decisions.q: The Mail tab looks like a personal mailbox with Inbox, Sent and Drafts. Is the intent a full email client connected to each person's Gmail or Outlook, only email into a channel, or nothing?
decisions.a: A Gmail-like interface where Toki itself sends and receives; no connection to Gmail; read and unread state. Later phase
decisions.options: (a) Client connected to Gmail/Outlook · (b) Email-into-channel only · (c) Drop

decisions.q: The prototype says summaries are made by 'Claude on this computer', only in the desktop app, with nothing passing through the Toki server. Keep that model, have the server call the Claude API with a company key, or decide later?
decisions.a: (a), built after the desktop app exists
decisions.options: (a) Claude on the user's computer · (b) Server calls the API · (c) Later

decisions.q: Who uses the first version, your own company or paying customers, and roughly how many people per workspace and online at once?
decisions.a: Internal first, up to about 200 people, one server
decisions.options: Internal or for sale; how many people

decisions.q: Who will build this, you alone with Claude or a team, and is there a deadline for the first release?
decisions.a: You alone, with Claude
decisions.options: Who builds; any deadline

decisions.q: The prototype has no sign-in screen for members, only the guest one. How do members sign in, and how are accounts created?
decisions.a: (b) 6-digit emailed code, no password, admin invitation only, 30-day session
decisions.options: (a) Password · (b) Emailed code · (c) Google SSO

decisions.q: The prototype shows Owner, Admin and ordinary members but no difference between them. Who is allowed to do what?
decisions.a: As in the capability table under Roles & States
decisions.options: What Member, Admin and Owner can do

decisions.q: Is there a time limit on editing a message, and what happens when a message that has a thread is deleted? The prototype deletes every reply too.
decisions.a: Edit without limit; soft delete that keeps the thread
decisions.options: Time limit; deleting a message that has a thread

decisions.q: Where are files stored, what is the size limit, and which previews are built: image thumbnails, PDFs, link previews?
decisions.a: (b) MinIO, 100 MB, image thumbnails, link previews
decisions.options: (a) Server disk · (b) S3 storage; size limit; previews

decisions.q: Ctrl+K searches conversations, people, messages and actions, and Vietnamese has to match when typed without diacritics. Use Postgres full-text search, or add a separate search engine?
decisions.a: (a), ignoring Vietnamese diacritics, respecting permissions
decisions.options: (a) Postgres full-text · (b) Meilisearch

decisions.q: The prototype has desktop notifications, sound, missed-mention email, per-channel levels, mute, Pause and Focus time. Which of these are in phase 1?
decisions.a: Badges, Web Push, sound, per-channel level, mute, Pause, Focus time. Missed-mention email later
decisions.options: Pick from the prototype's kinds

decisions.q: Which message features are in phase 1 and which wait? And what about three things the prototype does not have: @channel, a full emoji picker, and group DMs with several people?
decisions.a: As recommended; add @channel, group DMs up to 8, keep 8 fixed emoji
decisions.options: What is in, what waits, and three items not in the prototype

decisions.q: The prototype has two looks that differ in layout as well as colour, and two languages of which only the navigation is translated. Does phase 1 build both looks and both languages, and which language is the default?
decisions.a: Both Calm and Focus; full vi and en, English by default
decisions.options: One look or two; one language or two

decisions.q: Is this prototype the only design source, or is there a Figma file or a requirements document as well? How closely should it be followed?
decisions.a: The prototype is the only source; Claude decides what it does not draw
decisions.options: Prototype only, or also Figma

decisions.q: Where does the server run and who can reach it: a private network only, or the public internet on its own domain?
decisions.a: (b) Public, Docker Compose on one VPS
decisions.options: (a) Private network only · (b) Public

decisions.q: In what order should the phases after phase 1 come? Do you want to move, merge or split any of them?
decisions.a: As recommended; the phone app was later moved up to phase 3
decisions.options: A seven-phase roadmap

decisions.q: For the Mail phase: mail only between Toki members, or real mail where each person has an address on the company domain and writes to anyone outside?
decisions.a: (b) as recommended; details wait for the Mail phase
decisions.options: (a) Between members only · (b) With anyone outside

decisions.q: How should the work be run: where the repository lives, whether there is CI, how much testing, and how changes are reviewed?
decisions.a: Private GitHub, CI, test-first backend, Playwright, one PR per task group
decisions.options: Hosting, CI, test depth, review

decisions.q: You want web, desktop and phone to be built later without changing technology. Which interface technology should be shared across them?
decisions.a: P2: React for web and desktop, React Native for phone
decisions.options: P1 React + wrappers · P2 React + React Native · P3 React Native everywhere · P4 Flutter

decisions.q: How should the backend be organised, and why Node rather than Python, including the case where an AI chatbot is added later?
decisions.a: Modular monolith in Node and TypeScript; no Python
decisions.options: Modular monolith in Node · Next.js · Sync platform · Python

decisions.q: Now that the phone app will be React Native: does phase 1 build only the web app with the groundwork laid, or the web and phone apps side by side?
decisions.a: (a) Web first
decisions.topic: When to build the phone app
decisions.options: (a) Web first with the groundwork laid · (b) Both in phase 1

decisions.q: Sign-in by emailed code needs the server to send mail from phase 1. Which service should send it, and do you already have a domain?
decisions.a: Phase 1 sends through configurable SMTP. A dedicated service is decided in a later phase
decisions.options: Resend, Postmark, SES, a Google account, self-hosted

decisions.q: A fresh installation has no accounts. How does the first Owner come to exist?
decisions.a: Created from environment variables or seed; that admin invites members
decisions.options: First-run setup page, or environment

decisions.q: What do people who join a channel later see of its history, and what happens to a channel that is no longer used?
decisions.a: Full history; channels are archived, never deleted
decisions.options: What newcomers see; what happens to unused channels

decisions.q: On an iPhone, push notifications work only when the web app has been added to the Home Screen. Should the web app be an installable PWA?
decisions.a: Installable PWA; service worker for push only
decisions.options: Make it a PWA or not

decisions.q: Should the prototype's sample data (Hugepig Studio, 8 people, the sample channels and messages) be used as seed data?
decisions.a: Yes, for development and tests; production starts empty
decisions.options: Seed the prototype's data or not

decisions.q: The mail service decision was postponed, but sign-in by code depends on sending mail. How do people sign in during phase 1?
decisions.a: Withdrawn. D-011 stands: emailed codes
decisions.options: (a) Password · (b) Admin-issued link · (c) Keep emailed codes

decisions.q: How long may a display name be? The flow for accepting an invitation checked '1 to 80 characters' without a decision behind it.
decisions.a: 1 to 80 characters
decisions.options: A minimum and a maximum length

decisions.q: Which channel does everyone start in, and can it be left?
decisions.a: Every workspace has a #general channel created at setup; every member is in it automatically; it cannot be left or archived.

decisions.q: Which conversation does the app open on?
decisions.a: The app opens on the conversation last viewed on that device; the first time, on #general.

decisions.q: When does a person show as away, and is there an offline state?
decisions.a: Presence turns to Away after 5 minutes without activity. There is no separate Offline state.

decisions.q: How long does an invitation last, and does its link need a sign-in code?
decisions.a: An invitation expires after 7 days. The link in the invitation signs the person in directly, without a code.

decisions.q: How often may a sign-in code be requested, and when can it be sent again?
decisions.a: At most 5 code requests per email in 15 minutes; the resend button enables after 60 seconds.

decisions.q: Can there be several Owners, and what protects the last one?
decisions.a: There can be several Owners. The last Owner cannot be demoted or deactivated.

decisions.q: What may a channel name contain, and can a channel switch between public and private?
decisions.a: Channel names: lowercase letters, digits, hyphens, up to 80 characters, unique. Public cannot become private after creation, or the reverse.

decisions.q: Who may edit a channel's topic and use @channel?
decisions.a: Any channel member can edit the topic and use @channel; in a channel of 20 or more people, @channel asks for confirmation first.

decisions.q: How long may a message be, and how many files may it carry?
decisions.a: A message holds up to 10,000 characters and 10 files.

decisions.q: What happens to the files of a deleted message?
decisions.a: Deleting a message also removes its attached files from storage.

decisions.q: What does a push notification show?
decisions.a: A push notification shows the sender, the conversation and the start of the message.

decisions.q: Can people be added to or removed from a group DM?
decisions.a: People cannot be added to or removed from a group DM.

decisions.q: What is the default notification level?
decisions.a: Default notification level: 'Mentions only' for channels, 'All messages' for DMs.

decisions.q: Do Admins and Owners see and manage every conversation?
decisions.a: Admins and Owners do not automatically see private channels or DMs; deleting messages, removing people and archiving apply only where they are members.

decisions.q: Does a sender see who has read a message?
decisions.a: Toki has no 'seen' receipts; a sender does not know who has read a message.

decisions.q: What is shown when an admin deletes someone's message?
decisions.a: A message deleted by an admin shows as 'Message deleted by an admin' and its author is told.

decisions.q: Can a guest message members directly or start a Meet with them?
decisions.a: No. A guest stays inside the invited channel: no Message or Start a Meet button on profiles, no DMs, and only that channel's Meets. The server refuses any access outside the channel, with a dedicated permission test suite for guests.

decisions.q: After leaving a private channel, can a member rejoin alone or do they need an invitation?
decisions.a: A member must invite them back. The leave confirmation says so; Undo is still offered for 5 seconds. Private channels never appear in Browse or Ctrl+K for outsiders. If the last member leaves, the channel is archived.

decisions.q: What marks a channel as read on Web and Phone, and when does the New divider clear?
decisions.a: Read state never depends on AI. A conversation is read when it is open, the window is in use, and the person is at the bottom of the list. The New divider anchors to the first unread message at the time of opening (by ID, so it does not drift), stays while viewing, and is gone the next time the conversation opens. Opening the app or a conversation with unread messages scrolls to the divider.

decisions.q: Which features must reach the phone at launch?
decisions.a: All of phase 1. On narrow screens, global search, the account menu, status, Pause and Focus time live in the More sheet; Mark done and Snooze in Activity are always visible. AI summaries exist nowhere in phase 1.

decisions.q: What is the smallest supported window, and should the thread panel overlay the chat below some width?
decisions.a: Smallest is 360 × 560. From 720 to 1099px side panels overlay the chat. See rule D-068.

decisions.q: How far ahead does Calendar show, and may a scheduled Meet be edited, cancelled or set in the past?
decisions.a: Any distance ahead, by moving week or month. The creator and admins can edit and cancel; changes are posted to the channel. A start time in the past is rejected. After scheduling, Calendar jumps to that Meet's day.

decisions.q: What happens when a guest's access expires, and what does a repeat invitation do?
decisions.a: On expiry every guest session is revoked, the guest cannot sign in, and old messages stay with an 'expired' label; a member can extend access. Re-inviting the same email in the same channel updates the expiry instead of creating a second guest. A past expiry date is rejected; the year is always shown.

decisions.q: Can a member start a Meet in a channel they have not joined?
decisions.a: No. Pickers list only joined conversations. See rule D-077.

decisions.q: Should @mention suggest only channel members? What if a non-member is mentioned?
decisions.a: It suggests only members of that conversation, guests included, plus @channel. People outside the conversation are not suggested and not notified; to involve them, add them to the channel.

decisions.q: After an approval decision, who is notified, and can the approver change their mind?
decisions.a: The requester gets an Activity item. The approver is not notified of their own action, and the 'asked you to approve' item becomes done. The decision is final; to change it the requester sends a new request.

decisions.q: Which actions queue while offline and which are blocked?
decisions.a: Phase 1 has no offline mode: per rule D-079 only messages wait and resend. Phase 6 also queues reactions, edits, read markers and saves to Later. Always blocked offline: sending mail, joining a Meet, uploading files, inviting people, admin actions.

decisions.q: What is the standard pattern for destructive actions?
decisions.a: One or the other, depending on whether the action can be reversed. See rules D-069 and D-070. Undo: archive an email, mark done, leave a public channel, remove from Later, unpin. Confirm: delete a message, delete an automation, deactivate a member, archive a channel, cancel a Meet.

decisions.q: Is Mail a full client or a light reader for discussing email in channels?
decisions.a: A full client, per D-007 and D-022. Drafts reopen to edit, send or delete; there is an Archive folder; reply drafts are kept per email; folder counts are all the same kind of number; each folder has its own empty state.

decisions.q: Do reminders and calendar alerts break through Pause and Focus time?
decisions.a: No. Everything is held until it ends. See rule D-072.

decisions.q: How much of the interface must be in Vietnamese for the first release?
decisions.a: All of it, per D-018. CI fails when a string lacks a translation in either language.

decisions.q: Which roles can open Admin and manage automations?
decisions.a: The Admin page: Admin and Owner, per D-012. Analytics: Admin and Owner. A channel's automations: Admin, Owner and the channel's creator can create and edit; only Admin and Owner see the list of all automations.

decisions.q: Why are the Claude summaries desktop-only, and is a Web or Phone version planned?
decisions.a: Because per D-008 summaries run through Claude on the user's own computer, which needs the desktop app. Under that model there is no Web or Phone version. Having one would mean running AI on the server, which belongs to the open item on an AI chatbot in phase 6. On Web and Phone the interface shows no AI entry point, and read state never depends on AI.
No feature may be hover-only or desktop-only. Every action has an entry point on narrow and touch screens.

Smallest supported size is 360 × 560. Under 720px: one pane at a time. From 720 to 1099px: side panels (thread, details, profile) overlay the chat instead of squeezing it. From 1100px: three columns. Navigation and the tab row scroll when short of room; the conversation list is always the main area of the sidebar.

A reversible action happens at once and shows a toast with Undo for 5 seconds. An irreversible action, or one that affects other people, asks for confirmation and names its target. Never both for one action.
A form that has content does not close on an outside click; closing it by button asks whether to discard.
Your own action never notifies you. An Activity item becomes done on its own once the thing it asks for is done. Activity is newest first and has a filter chip for every kind of item.

During Pause or Focus time there is no toast, push or sound, including reminders you set yourself. Badges still update. When it ends, one summary lists what arrived. Starting Focus during Focus extends it rather than nesting; ending restores the earlier status.

Dates and times: required fields cannot be left empty; where a future time is needed the past is rejected; the year is shown whenever it is not the current year; one format across the app; 'Invalid Date' never appears.
Every searchable or filterable list has an empty state centred in the content area and written for that context. A count on a chip always equals the rows shown.
Every icon-only button has a name for screen readers (lint checks it). A modal traps focus and returns it to the opening button. Menus work with arrow keys.
After something is created, the screen shows it; if a filter would hide it, the filter changes.
Writing to a conversation (sending, starting a Meet, scheduling) requires membership. Pickers list only conversations you have joined.
Toasts and floating bars never cover the composer or navigation.

When the connection drops: loaded content stays readable; messages being sent wait and send themselves when the connection returns; every other action is blocked with an explanation, never a false success.

decisions.q: Someone is signed in as A and presses an invitation or sign-in link meant for B. Does the link replace A's session, or does the page ask first?
decisions.a: Ask first: 'You are signed in as A. Continue as B?'

decisions.q: What does the invitation refusal page say, and does it tell the causes apart?
decisions.a: Three messages. **Expired:** 'This invitation expired on 12 Nov. Ask Minh to send a new one.' **Revoked:** 'This invitation is no longer valid. Ask an admin of Hugepig Studio for a new one.' **Unknown or damaged link:** 'This link is not valid.', with no workspace name. An invitation already used goes to the sign-in page with the email filled in. No page has a sign-in button for a stranger.

decisions.q: The prototype's code screen has no Resend, only 'Use a different email'. D-038 already expects a Resend button after 60 seconds. Is Resend added to the screen, and does a new code cancel the earlier one?
decisions.a: Yes: 'Resend code' under the field, greyed with a countdown for 60 seconds. A new code cancels the earlier one, so only the newest mail works.

decisions.q: The welcome step after accepting an invitation is not in the prototype. Is it wanted, and with which fields?
decisions.a: One screen: display name (required, 1 to 80, filled from the address), job title (optional), time zone (from the device). 'Enter Toki' and 'Skip'.

decisions.q: **Your finding:** the prototype has no '+' for a new channel, only '+ Browse channels', and Browse channels has nothing to create one. Where does 'Create channel' live?
decisions.a: (a) A 'Create channel' button at the top of Browse channels, a 'Create channel' command in Ctrl+K, and 'Create #text' when a search finds nothing · (b) A separate '+' beside the Conversations heading. Suggested: (a), as written flow F20 says.

decisions.q: Can an Owner or Admin remove a member from any channel? Decided so far (D-047): no, only from a channel they belong to, and never from #general. Does that stand, and can the creator of a channel remove people too?
decisions.a: Keep D-047. The creator has no extra right. The removed person gets an Activity item 'Lan removed you from #name'; the channel shows 'Lan removed Minh'. This flow has no chart yet.

decisions.q: How does a person choose several people for a group DM? The prototype's New message dialog opens a conversation on the first press.
decisions.a: Each press adds the person as a chip in the field; a 'Start' button opens the conversation. One chip plus Enter opens the DM. Channels in the list still open at once. Limit stays 8 with you (D-017).

decisions.q: The prototype shows 'Waiting to send' and nothing for a send that failed. Where do 'Not sent', Retry and Delete appear?
decisions.a: In the same place as 'Waiting to send', beside the time: a red 'Not sent' followed by two text buttons, Retry and Delete. The message stays faded. Delete asks nothing, since nobody else has seen it.

decisions.q: Does a mention notify the person when the conversation is muted?
decisions.a: (a) A personal switch, on by default · (b) Never · (c) Always Suggested: (a), as in the prototype

decisions.q: Does every conversation, thread and section have its own address, and what does browser Back do?
decisions.a: (a) Each has an address; Back closes the side panel first, then returns to the previous place · (b) One address for the whole app Suggested: (a)

decisions.q: Is the capability matrix on the Roles & States tab the agreed authority for what Members and Admins see?
decisions.a: (a) Yes, sign it off as is · (b) Review it row by row first Suggested: (b)

decisions.q: The 51 written flows were drafted by Claude under decision D-019 ('Claude decides what the prototype does not draw'). Several things in them were never asked one by one: Sign out and the list of signed-in devices (F06), Resend and Revoke of an invitation (F02), what deactivation does to a person's messages and DMs (F41). Are the written flows accepted as the baseline, or reviewed group by group first?
decisions.a: Review the four phase-1 groups that have no prototype screen (account and sign-in, channels, administration, status); accept the rest as written.

decisions.q: No decision on backup and recovery: how often data is backed up, and how much may be lost or how long the service may be down.
decisions.a: Nightly backup of database and files to another place, kept 14 days; a restore tested before launch.

decisions.q: Sign out in one tab: do the other tabs of the same browser leave at once?
decisions.a: Yes, at once; they share the session

decisions.q: An Admin invites the address of a deactivated member. Refuse, or offer Reactivate?
decisions.a: Refuse with 'This account is deactivated' and a Reactivate button

decisions.q: Are any file types refused (for example programs), or is every type accepted up to 100 MB?
decisions.a: Accept every type; always download, never run in the browser

decisions.q: A message is deleted while someone else is writing a reply in its thread. Is the reply still sent?
decisions.a: Yes; the thread stays under the 'Message deleted' line

decisions.q: How long does a 'Waiting to send' message keep trying before it becomes 'Not sent'?
decisions.a: It waits while offline; once online, one automatic try, then 'Not sent' with Retry

decisions.q: Can a member change their own sign-in address, or only an Admin?
decisions.a: Nobody in phase 1; an Owner does it later

decisions.q: A batch of invitations fails halfway (the mail server goes down after 3 of 10). Keep the 3, or undo all?
decisions.a: Keep them; each row reports its own result

decisions.q: #general exists before anyone is invited and every newcomer is in it (D-034). Does #general show a line when someone joins, and does that line notify anyone?
decisions.a: Yes: a grey system line 'Minh joined', with the date. It raises no unread count and no notification. The prototype has no system lines; its sample shows a person writing 'Welcome Jordan to the team!'.

decisions.q: Which fields does the Create channel dialog have, and what are their limits?
decisions.a: Name (rule D-040), Private switch (off by default), Topic (optional, up to 250 characters), Add people (optional). Written flow F20 has 'add members'; the chart leaves it out until you confirm.

decisions.q: The prototype's offline banner reads 'Offline: showing saved messages'. Written flow F37 said 'Reconnecting…' and a 'Reconnected' toast, which the prototype does not have. Which wording, and is there a separate reconnecting state?
decisions.a: (a) Keep the prototype's banner the whole time; it disappears when the connection is back, with no toast · (b) Same banner, plus the words 'Reconnecting…' during each try · (c) Replace it by 'Reconnecting…'. Suggested: (a). Until answered the charts use (a) (D-140).

decisions.q: What is the difference between the level 'Nothing' and Mute?
decisions.a: (a) Level decides toast, push and sound; Mute also hides the unread badge and bold · (b) Remove 'Nothing', keep Mute · (c) Remove Mute Suggested: (a)

decisions.q: Where do form errors appear: under the field with the button disabled, or in a toast after pressing?
decisions.a: (a) Under the field; button disabled until valid · (b) Toast after pressing, as the prototype Suggested: (a)

decisions.q: Can a channel be renamed, and who edits its description?
decisions.a: (a) No rename in phase 1; any member edits topic and description · (b) Admins and the creator rename Suggested: (a)

decisions.q: What happens when storage runs out or reaches a quota?
decisions.a: (a) No quota; Owners are warned at 80% of the disk; uploads refused at 95% · (b) A fixed quota per workspace Suggested: (a)

decisions.q: What does an open app do when a new version is deployed?
decisions.a: (a) Strip 'Update available · Reload'; forced only when the server says the page is too old · (b) Silent reload when idle Suggested: (a)

decisions.q: Which browsers are supported?
decisions.a: (a) The last two versions of Chrome, Edge, Safari, Firefox; iPhone push only when installed to the home screen · (b) Chrome and Edge only Suggested: (a)

decisions.q: How do member lists and people pickers behave at 200 people?
decisions.a: (a) Search field on top, first 50 shown, more on scroll · (b) Show all Suggested: (a)

decisions.q: Are administrative actions recorded, and can anyone see the record?
decisions.a: (a) Recorded on the server, no screen in phase 1 · (b) A screen for Owners · (c) Not recorded Suggested: (a)

decisions.q: How is a double press prevented for creating a channel, sending invitations and setting a reminder?
decisions.a: (a) Button disabled while the request runs, and the server ignores a repeat of the same request · (b) Button disabled only Suggested: (a)

decisions.q: What does search cover, and how much does it return?
decisions.a: (a) Ctrl+K: conversations, people, commands, then messages; 20 results per kind, more on request · (b) Messages only in a separate search page Suggested: (a)

decisions.q: The phase-1 acceptance criteria list six performance targets (message seen by another person: p95 under 150 ms; first load on 4G under 2 s; initial JavaScript under 200 KB; switching to an opened channel under 100 ms; 60 frames per second scrolling 10,000 messages; search over 1 million messages p95 under 200 ms). Claude proposed them; they were never put to you as a question. Are they the targets?
decisions.a: Accept them as written, with 200 people online as the load (D-009).

decisions.q: 'Today 15:00' in the reminder menu after 15:00: hidden, or replaced by another choice?
decisions.a: Hidden; 'In 3 hours' takes its place

decisions.q: Two people create a channel with the same name at the same moment.
decisions.a: The second gets '#name already exists' with a button to open it (already in the chart; confirm)

decisions.q: Does previewing a public channel without joining count for its unread or Activity?
decisions.a: No; a preview leaves no trace

decisions.q: Should the first load have a size limit for very large workspaces (how many conversations come with `GET /bootstrap`)?
decisions.a: All of them in phase 1; revisit past 500 conversations

decisions.q: Can a person upload a profile picture in phase 1?
decisions.a: (a) Initials only in phase 1 · (b) Upload in phase 1 Suggested: (a)

decisions.q: Can a person stop following a thread?
decisions.a: (a) 'Unfollow thread' in the thread menu · (b) Not in phase 1 Suggested: (a)

decisions.q: Is 'Mark as unread' in phase 1?
decisions.a: (a) Later phase · (b) Phase 1 Suggested: (a); Later covers the need

decisions.q: Two people change the same topic, status or task at the same moment. Who wins?
decisions.a: (a) The last save wins and everyone sees it live · (b) The second save is refused with 'This changed' Suggested: (a) for short fields; (b) for long text later

decisions.q: Does the browser tab show unread messages?
decisions.a: (a) '(3) Toki' counting mentions and DMs, a dot for anything else · (b) Nothing Suggested: (a)

decisions.q: 24-hour time for everyone, or by language?
decisions.a: (a) 24-hour everywhere · (b) Follows the language · (c) A setting Suggested: (a)

decisions.q: Can a workspace export its data (messages, files)?
decisions.a: (a) Server backup only in phase 1 · (b) An export for Owners Suggested: (a)

decisions.q: Endpoint names and shapes in the charts (`POST /auth/code-requests`, `GET /bootstrap`, `PUT /conversations/:id/read` and the rest) are proposals. All sit under `/api/v1`.
decisions.a: Names are fixed in the spec of each ticket

decisions.q: A request with no answer after 10 seconds counts as failed and shows Retry.
decisions.a: Any value between 8 and 15 s works

decisions.q: Typing a space in a channel name turns it into a hyphen, and capitals into lowercase, instead of showing an error.
decisions.a: Fewer errors for the same rule

decisions.q: The uniqueness of a channel name includes archived channels.
decisions.a: Otherwise un-archiving could collide

decisions.q: Reconnect attempts wait 1, 2, 5, 10 and then 30 seconds, with a little randomness.
decisions.a: Avoids every client retrying at once

decisions.q: A file uploaded but never sent is deleted from storage after 24 hours.
decisions.a: Keeps storage clean

decisions.q: Server status codes map to screens as in flow 3.3: 400 field message, 403 and 404 one shared page, 409 and 410 fresh copy, 429 wait, 5xx Retry with an error ID.
decisions.a: One behaviour for every feature

decisions.q: A 'Waiting to send' message survives a page reload, kept in the browser, and is dropped if someone else signs in on that browser.
decisions.a: Needed for the 'nothing lost' promise

decisions.q: Leaving a channel clears its unread count and its open Activity items for that person.
decisions.a: Otherwise items point to a place they cannot open

decisions.q: Batches of invitations are limited to 50 addresses.
decisions.a: Protects the mail account's sending limit

decisions.q: A mention of someone who is not in the channel creates no notification; the sender is offered 'Add them'.
decisions.a: Matches rule BR-09

decisions.q: A member's sign-in code is valid for 10 minutes.
decisions.a: The prototype's guest code screen says 'It works for 10 minutes'; nothing decides it for members

decisions.q: A code is cancelled after 5 wrong tries; the person asks for a new one.
decisions.a: A 6-digit code must not be guessable; the prototype accepts any 6 digits

decisions.q: A session renews on every use, so 30 days means 30 days without opening Toki.
decisions.a: D-011 fixes 30 days but not whether it counts from sign-in or from last use

decisions.q: Every screen and every wording in quotes that the prototype does not contain is a proposal: 'Session ended', 'Account deactivated', 'Not found or no access', 'Not sent', 'Can't reach Toki', loading placeholders, and the rest.
decisions.a: The charts need a name for each state; the design decides the final words

decisions.q: While offline the banner keeps the prototype's words, 'Offline: showing saved messages'. A separate 'Reconnecting…' state is not assumed.
decisions.a: The prototype shows only this banner; see D-102

decisions.q: Everything a Member or Admin sees follows the capability matrix; the prototype shows only an Owner.
decisions.a: Account card: 'Owner'

decisions.q: Notification preferences belong to the person and apply on every device; only the browser's permission for push is per device.
decisions.a: Preferences shows one set of switches

decisions.q: Star and Mute are personal: nobody else sees them, and starred conversations sort to the top of that person's list.
decisions.a: Details panel; starred glyph in the list

decisions.q: The local time shown on a profile comes from the time zone the person set, not from where they are now.
decisions.a: Profile: local time and a city

decisions.q: Demo-only controls never ship: the Look / Device / Clock / Guide bar, 'Reset', and every '20 seconds (demo)' choice.
decisions.a: Marked 'demo' in the prototype

decisions.q: The pink 'New' pills mark proposed features, not states of the product.
decisions.a: Switch 'Highlight proposed features'

decisions.q: Sample people, channels and messages are illustration only; no seed content ships except #general.
decisions.a: Sample workspace 'Hugepig Studio'

decisions.q: Analytics never names private channels or DMs and hides any group smaller than three.
decisions.a: Admin: 'Private channels and direct messages', 'fewer than 3'

charts.title: 1.1 The whole app on one page: ways in, the gate, and what a signed-in person can reach
notes: **Entry points (4):** the Toki address, a link to a conversation or message (from a notification, a mail or a colleague), the installed app icon, and the invitation mail.
**One gate:** every way in passes the session check. Nothing in Toki is readable without a session; there is no public page besides sign-in.
**Role check:** Admin is the only section gated by role. Everything else is gated by membership of the conversation, checked on the server for every request.

**In the prototype:** It opens straight into Home as Lan, an Owner. There is no sign-in, invitation, welcome or refusal page for members. The only sign-in screens belong to the guest portal (phase 5; demo guide → 'View as guest'): an email step, then a code step that says 'It works for 10 minutes'. Ctrl K exists: the Search box at the top of the left sidebar carries the label 'Ctrl K', and the keys open the command palette. Admin exists in the left navigation but holds only analytics and automations.
sources: How long does an invitation last, and does its link need a sign-in code? (D-037)
You confirmed: An invitation expires after 7 days. The link in the invitation signs the person in directly, without a code.
The prototype has no sign-in screen for members, only the guest one. How do members sign in, and how are accounts created? (D-011)
You chose the recommended option: (b) 6-digit emailed code, no password, admin invitation only, 30-day session
The prototype shows Owner, Admin and ordinary members but no difference between them. Who is allowed to do what? (D-012)
You chose the recommended option: As in the capability table under Roles & States
**Assumed, not confirmed (D-136):** A member's sign-in code is valid for 10 minutes.
**Assumed, not confirmed (D-138):** A session renews on every use, so 30 days means 30 days without opening Toki.

charts.title: 1.2 Exit points: every way a person stops being in the app
notes: Only **Sign out** and **deactivation** end the session on purpose. Closing the tab never does.
Losing the connection is not an exit: the person stays on the same screen, read-only, until it returns (flow 3.1).

**In the prototype:** Sign out is not in the prototype. The account menu holds Set status, Pause notifications, Focus time and Preferences only (finding N-04). There are no sessions, so 'Session ended' and 'Account deactivated' do not exist either. Offline is a demo switch.
sources: The prototype has no sign-in screen for members, only the guest one. How do members sign in, and how are accounts created? (D-011)
You chose the recommended option: (b) 6-digit emailed code, no password, admin invitation only, 30-day session
The prototype shows Owner, Admin and ordinary members but no difference between them. Who is allowed to do what? (D-012)
You chose the recommended option: As in the capability table under Roles & States

**Rule D-079** (made from GAP-21 · D-060): When the connection drops: loaded content stays readable; messages being sent wait and send themselves when the connection returns; every other action is blocked with an explanation, never a false success.

**Assumed, not confirmed (D-139):** Every screen and every wording in quotes that the prototype does not contain is a proposal: 'Session ended', 'Account deactivated', 'Not found or no access', 'Not sent', 'Can't reach Toki', loading placeholders, and the rest.

charts.title: 2.1 Sign in with an emailed code
notes: **Before:** the address belongs to an active member; this device has no valid session.
**After:** a 30-day session on this device only; the code can never be used again; the app opens where the person was heading.

**Validation:** email must look like an address before the button enables. Code: exactly 6 digits, one use. Valid 10 minutes and cancelled after 5 wrong tries are assumptions (D-136, D-137). At most 5 code requests per address in 15 minutes (D-038).
**Back / cancel / retry:** 'Use a different email' returns to the email field. 'Resend code' enables after 60 seconds. A network failure re-enables the button with 'Could not connect'.
**Alternative:** the mail also has a sign-in button. Pressing it signs in the device where it is pressed and skips typing the code.
**Security rule:** the answer to a code request is identical for members and strangers, so the page never reveals who is a member.

**In the prototype:** No member sign-in. The nearest screens are the guest portal's: 'Sign in as a guest' (email, 'Email me a code') and 'Check your email' (6-digit field, 'Sign in', 'Use a different email', 'It works for 10 minutes'). That screen has **no Resend**, no limit on requests and no wrong-code state (any 6 digits work). Its two errors show in a red line under the card.
sources: The prototype has no sign-in screen for members, only the guest one. How do members sign in, and how are accounts created? (D-011)
You chose the recommended option: (b) 6-digit emailed code, no password, admin invitation only, 30-day session
How often may a sign-in code be requested, and when can it be sent again? (D-038)
You confirmed: At most 5 code requests per email in 15 minutes; the resend button enables after 60 seconds.
**Technical design:** A code request is answered the same way for members and strangers, so the page never reveals who is a member.
**Assumed, not confirmed (D-136):** A member's sign-in code is valid for 10 minutes.
**Assumed, not confirmed (D-137):** A code is cancelled after 5 wrong tries; the person asks for a new one.

charts.title: 2.2 Accept an invitation (first time in)
notes: **Before:** an Admin or Owner sent an invitation to this address (flow 2.12).
**After:** the member is Active, in #general with its full history, signed in on this device; the link no longer works; #general shows 'X joined'.
**Validation:** display name 1 to 80 characters (your answer, D-033). Time zone and language come from the device and can be changed.
**Skip:** the welcome step can be skipped; the name becomes the part of the address before @.
**Next:** a small card asks whether to turn on notifications.
**In the prototype:** Nothing. The only invitation in the prototype is 'Invite a client' for guests, in a channel's Details panel. There is no welcome step and no refusal page.
sources: The prototype has no sign-in screen for members, only the guest one. How do members sign in, and how are accounts created? (D-011)
You chose the recommended option: (b) 6-digit emailed code, no password, admin invitation only, 30-day session
A fresh installation has no accounts. How does the first Owner come to exist? (D-028)
Your answer: Created from environment variables or seed; that admin invites members
How long does an invitation last, and does its link need a sign-in code? (D-037)
You confirmed: An invitation expires after 7 days. The link in the invitation signs the person in directly, without a code.
Which channel does everyone start in, and can it be left? (D-034)
You confirmed: Every workspace has a #general channel created at setup; every member is in it automatically; it cannot be left or archived.
How long may a display name be? The flow for accepting an invitation checked '1 to 80 characters' without a decision behind it. (D-033)
Your answer: 1 to 80 characters

charts.title: 2.3 Open the app: session check and first load
notes: **Before:** none. This is where every entry point lands.
**After:** the sidebar, unread counts and one conversation are on screen, and the realtime connection is open.
**Loading:** the app frame appears at once with grey placeholders for the lists; real content replaces them.
**Rule:** a link to something the person may not see answers exactly like a link to something that does not exist.
**Rule:** with no link, the app opens the conversation last viewed on this device; the very first time, #general.
**In the prototype:** Everything is in memory, so the app appears at once. There are no placeholders, no 'Can't reach Toki', and the address does not change with the screen (findings N-05, N-13).
sources: Which conversation does the app open on? (D-035)
You confirmed: The app opens on the conversation last viewed on that device; the first time, on #general.
The prototype has no sign-in screen for members, only the guest one. How do members sign in, and how are accounts created? (D-011)
You chose the recommended option: (b) 6-digit emailed code, no password, admin invitation only, 30-day session
**Technical design:** 'Not found' and 'no access' get the same answer, so the app never confirms that a private thing exists.
**Assumed, not confirmed (D-126):** A request with no answer after 10 seconds counts as failed and shows Retry.

**Assumed, not confirmed (D-139):** Every screen and every wording in quotes that the prototype does not contain is a proposal: 'Session ended', 'Account deactivated', 'Not found or no access', 'Not sent', 'Can't reach Toki', loading placeholders, and the rest.

charts.title: 2.4 Open and read a conversation
notes: **Before:** signed in; a member of the conversation, or it is a public channel being previewed.
**After:** the read pointer sits on the newest message seen; the badge is cleared on every device of this person. Nobody else is told (no 'seen' receipts).
**Rule:** a conversation is marked read only when its newest message is on screen and the tab has focus. Opening it in a background tab changes nothing.
**Older messages:** scrolling up loads 50 more with a spinner at the top and keeps the scroll position; at the start a 'Beginning of #name' marker shows.
**Load failure:** the message area shows 'Couldn't load messages' with Retry; the sidebar keeps working (flow 3.3).
**Preview:** a public channel the person has not joined is readable; the composer is replaced by a Join button.
**In the prototype:** Home: the conversation list, the message list, unread badges and the 'New' divider exist. There is no loading state and no failure state.
sources: What marks a channel as read on Web and Phone, and when does the New divider clear? (D-052)

Answer: Read state never depends on AI. A conversation is read when it is open, the window is in use, and the person is at the bottom of the list. The New divider anchors to the first unread message at the time of opening (by ID, so it does not drift), stays while viewing, and is gone the next time the conversation opens. Opening the app or a conversation with unread messages scrolls to the divider.
Does a sender see who has read a message? (D-048)
You confirmed: Toki has no 'seen' receipts; a sender does not know who has read a message.
What do people who join a channel later see of its history, and what happens to a channel that is no longer used? (D-029)
You chose the recommended option: Full history; channels are archived, never deleted

**Rule D-074** (made from GAP-29, 31, 33): Every searchable or filterable list has an empty state centred in the content area and written for that context. A count on a chip always equals the rows shown.

**Assumed, not confirmed (D-139):** Every screen and every wording in quotes that the prototype does not contain is a proposal: 'Session ended', 'Account deactivated', 'Not found or no access', 'Not sent', 'Can't reach Toki', loading placeholders, and the rest.

charts.title: 2.5 Send a message
notes: **Before:** a member of the conversation; it is not archived; the composer holds 1 to 10,000 characters or at least one uploaded file.
**After:** one message stored exactly once; every member's unread count rises except the sender's; mentions become Activity items (flow 2.7); the draft is cleared on all devices.
**Disabled:** Send does nothing while the text is empty or only spaces, is locked past 10,000 characters (a counter appears near the limit), and while a file is still uploading.
**Keys:** Enter sends, Shift+Enter makes a new line; while composing a Vietnamese word, Enter finishes the word and does not send.
**Retry:** 'Not sent' offers Retry and Delete. Retry resends the same ID, so a message that did arrive is never doubled.
**Leaving mid-way:** switching conversation before sending keeps the text as a draft, synced to other devices.

**In the prototype:** The composer and Send exist. With the demo offline switch on, a sent message appears faded with 'Waiting to send'. **'Not sent', Retry and Delete are not in the prototype** (the words do not occur in it), and there is no character counter.
sources: How long may a message be, and how many files may it carry? (D-042)
You confirmed: A message holds up to 10,000 characters and 10 files.
**Rule D-077** (made from GAP-17 · D-057): Writing to a conversation (sending, starting a Meet, scheduling) requires membership. Pickers list only conversations you have joined.

**Rule D-079** (made from GAP-21 · D-060): When the connection drops: loaded content stays readable; messages being sent wait and send themselves when the connection returns; every other action is blocked with an explanation, never a false success.
**Technical design:** The app creates the message ID, so sending the same message again cannot create a second one.
**Assumed, not confirmed (D-126):** A request with no answer after 10 seconds counts as failed and shows Retry.

charts.title: 2.6 Attach files to a message
notes: **Before:** a conversation the person can write to; online (uploading is blocked offline).
**After:** each file is stored once and attached to the message; it appears in the conversation's 'Files & links' tab and in Files; only people who can see the conversation can open it.
**Validation:** at most 10 files per message, 100 MB each. A refused file is named in the message; the others continue.
**Cancel:** × on a card stops that upload and removes the card. Deleting the whole draft removes every card.
**Loading:** a thumbnail that is not ready shows a placeholder of the right proportions, so the list does not jump.

**In the prototype:** The paperclip in the composer adds a finished sample file at once. There is no file picker, progress bar, limit or failure (finding N-07). The numbers 10 and 100 MB appear nowhere in the prototype.
sources: How long may a message be, and how many files may it carry? (D-042)
You confirmed: A message holds up to 10,000 characters and 10 files.
Where are files stored, what is the size limit, and which previews are built: image thumbnails, PDFs, link previews? (D-014)
You chose the recommended option: (b) MinIO, 100 MB, image thumbnails, link previews
**Rule D-077** (made from GAP-17 · D-057): Writing to a conversation (sending, starting a Meet, scheduling) requires membership. Pickers list only conversations you have joined.
**Assumed, not confirmed (D-130):** A file uploaded but never sent is deleted from storage after 24 hours.

charts.title: 2.7 Being mentioned: from the sender's @ to the recipient reading it
notes: **Before:** the message was sent (flow 2.5) and contains @person, @channel or @here.
**After:** the recipient has one Activity item; it becomes done by itself once the message has been opened.
**Rule:** your own action never notifies you.
**Rule:** during Pause or Focus there is no toast, push or sound; badges still update, and one summary lists what arrived when it ends.

**Open:** a mention always gets through the 'Mentions only' level. Whether it gets through Mute is not decided (question D-088 on the Gap analysis tab); the chart shows the muted case as badge only until it is.
**Rule:** @channel in a channel of 20 or more people asks the sender to confirm first.
**Edit:** adding a mention by editing notifies the new person; removing one removes the earlier notification.

**In the prototype:** The @ button and the people picker are in the composer; Activity lists mentions; Pause and Focus time are in the account menu; Preferences has 'Notify me for @mentions even in muted channels'. Push and the recipient's side cannot be observed: only one person is simulated.
sources: The prototype has desktop notifications, sound, missed-mention email, per-channel levels, mute, Pause and Focus time. Which of these are in phase 1? (D-016)
You chose the recommended option: Badges, Web Push, sound, per-channel level, mute, Pause, Focus time. Missed-mention email later

**Rule D-071** (made from GAP-20, 26 · D-059): Your own action never notifies you. An Activity item becomes done on its own once the thing it asks for is done. Activity is newest first and has a filter chip for every kind of item.

**Rule D-072** (made from GAP-25, 38 · D-063): During Pause or Focus time there is no toast, push or sound, including reminders you set yourself. Badges still update. When it ends, one summary lists what arrived. Starting Focus during Focus extends it rather than nesting; ending restores the earlier status.
What is the default notification level? (D-046)
You confirmed: Default notification level: 'Mentions only' for channels, 'All messages' for DMs.
Who may edit a channel's topic and use @channel? (D-041)
You confirmed: Any channel member can edit the topic and use @channel; in a channel of 20 or more people, @channel asks for confirmation first.
What does a push notification show? (D-044)
You confirmed: A push notification shows the sender, the conversation and the start of the message.
**Assumed, not confirmed (D-135):** A mention of someone who is not in the channel creates no notification; the sender is offered 'Add them'.

charts.title: 2.8 Create a channel
notes: **Before:** signed in as Member, Admin or Owner.
**After:** the channel exists, the creator is its only member, it is open on screen and listed in the sidebar.
**Validation:** lowercase letters, digits and hyphens, up to 80 characters, unique among all channels including archived ones. Public or private is chosen here and cannot be changed later.
**Cancel:** Cancel, Esc or the × asks 'Discard this channel?' if anything was typed; an outside click does nothing.
**Rule:** after creating, the screen shows the new thing.

**In the prototype:** **A channel cannot be created in the prototype.** The sidebar has a '#' icon and a '+ Browse channels' row; both open Browse channels, which has a search field and Join or Open per row, and nothing to create a channel (finding N-03).
sources: The prototype shows Owner, Admin and ordinary members but no difference between them. Who is allowed to do what? (D-012)
You chose the recommended option: As in the capability table under Roles & States
What may a channel name contain, and can a channel switch between public and private? (D-040)
You confirmed: Channel names: lowercase letters, digits, hyphens, up to 80 characters, unique. Public cannot become private after creation, or the reverse.
**Rule D-070** (made from GAP-22 · D-061): A form that has content does not close on an outside click; closing it by button asks whether to discard.
**Rule D-076** (made from GAP-13, 14, 38): After something is created, the screen shows it; if a filter would hide it, the filter changes.
**Assumed, not confirmed (D-127):** Typing a space in a channel name turns it into a hyphen, and capitals into lowercase, instead of showing an error.
**Assumed, not confirmed (D-128):** The uniqueness of a channel name includes archived channels.

charts.title: 2.9 Join a public channel, and leave a channel
notes: **Before (join):** the channel is public and not archived. Private channels are joined only by being added.
**After (join):** member with full history; 'X joined' line in the channel; toast 'Joined #name'.
**After (leave):** the channel leaves the sidebar; its unread and Activity items are cleared; 'X left' line in the channel.
**Rule:** #general cannot be left. A reversible action shows Undo for 5 seconds; an irreversible one asks for confirmation; never both.
**Empty and archived:** no match shows 'No channels match' and a Create button carrying the search text; archived channels are listed with a View button only.

**In the prototype:** Browse channels (search, Join, Open) exists. Leaving is in the Details panel: 'Leave channel', then 'Leave #name? You can rejoin from Browse channels.', then a toast with Undo, for public and private alike (finding N-09). Removing someone else from a channel does not exist.
sources: Which channel does everyone start in, and can it be left? (D-034)
You confirmed: Every workspace has a #general channel created at setup; every member is in it automatically; it cannot be left or archived.

**Rule D-069** (made from GAP-24 · D-061): A reversible action happens at once and shows a toast with Undo for 5 seconds. An irreversible action, or one that affects other people, asks for confirmation and names its target. Never both for one action.
After leaving a private channel, can a member rejoin alone or do they need an invitation? (D-051)

Answer: A member must invite them back. The leave confirmation says so; Undo is still offered for 5 seconds. Private channels never appear in Browse or Ctrl+K for outsiders. If the last member leaves, the channel is archived.
What do people who join a channel later see of its history, and what happens to a channel that is no longer used? (D-029)
You chose the recommended option: Full history; channels are archived, never deleted
Do Admins and Owners see and manage every conversation? (D-047)
You confirmed: Admins and Owners do not automatically see private channels or DMs; deleting messages, removing people and archiving apply only where they are members.
**Assumed, not confirmed (D-133):** Leaving a channel clears its unread count and its open Activity items for that person.

charts.title: 2.10 Edit or delete your own message
notes: **Before:** the person is the author and the message is not deleted. There is no time limit.
**After (edit):** new text with '(edited)' beside the time; no history of earlier versions is kept.
**After (delete):** gone for everyone; attached files are removed from storage and from Files. A message with replies leaves a 'Message deleted' line and keeps its thread.
**Cancel:** Esc or Cancel leaves the message untouched. Save is disabled while the text is unchanged; saving an empty text offers Delete instead.
**Others:** Admins and Owners can delete other people's messages only in conversations they belong to; the author is told.

**In the prototype:** The More menu on your own message has Edit and Delete. Edit turns the text into a field with Save and Cancel and adds '(edited)'. Deleting a message with a thread removes every reply in the prototype.
sources: Is there a time limit on editing a message, and what happens when a message that has a thread is deleted? The prototype deletes every reply too. (D-013)
You chose the recommended option: Edit without limit; soft delete that keeps the thread
What happens to the files of a deleted message? (D-043)
You confirmed: Deleting a message also removes its attached files from storage.
Do Admins and Owners see and manage every conversation? (D-047)
You confirmed: Admins and Owners do not automatically see private channels or DMs; deleting messages, removing people and archiving apply only where they are members.
What is shown when an admin deletes someone's message? (D-049)
You confirmed: A message deleted by an admin shows as 'Message deleted by an admin' and its author is told.

**Rule D-069** (made from GAP-24 · D-061): A reversible action happens at once and shows a toast with Undo for 5 seconds. An irreversible action, or one that affects other people, asks for confirmation and names its target. Never both for one action.

charts.title: 2.11 Save for Later and set a reminder
notes: **Before:** the person can read the message.
**After:** the item is in Later under 'In progress'; with a reminder, a job is scheduled for that time; ticking the box moves it to Completed.
**Validation:** a reminder time must be in the future; a choice that is already past is not offered.
**Undo:** saving and un-saving are instant and reversible from the same bookmark; the toast 'Saved for Later' has a View button.
**Rule:** a count on a chip always equals the rows shown, including rows whose message was deleted.
**Empty:** with nothing saved, Later shows a centred note on how to save a message.
**In the prototype:** The bookmark on a message, the Later section, 'Remind me' or 'Change' on each row with a menu of times, and 'Remind me about this' in the message menu all exist.
sources: The prototype holds 14 feature groups. Which of them must be in the first release? (D-002)
You chose the recommended option: Core chat, Activity, Later, Files, People, Preferences, command palette

**Rule D-073** (made from GAP-12, 13, 16, 38): Dates and times: required fields cannot be left empty; where a future time is needed the past is rejected; the year is shown whenever it is not the current year; one format across the app; 'Invalid Date' never appears.

**Rule D-072** (made from GAP-25, 38 · D-063): During Pause or Focus time there is no toast, push or sound, including reminders you set yourself. Badges still update. When it ends, one summary lists what arrived. Starting Focus during Focus extends it rather than nesting; ending restores the earlier status.

**Rule D-074** (made from GAP-29, 31, 33): Every searchable or filterable list has an empty state centred in the content area and written for that context. A count on a chip always equals the rows shown.

charts.title: 2.12 Admin: invite members
notes: **Before:** signed in as Admin or Owner.
**After:** each new address has an 'Invited' row with its expiry date and an invitation mail on its way; nothing is created twice.
**Validation:** every entry must look like an address; duplicates inside the batch are merged.
**Authorization:** checked on the server for every admin request; hiding the menu item is not the check.
**Row actions:** Resend sends a fresh link and restarts the 7 days; Revoke asks for confirmation and kills the old link at once.
**Mail down:** the row says 'Mail not sent' and the server command for emergency access still works.

**In the prototype:** **Not in the prototype.** Admin (the shield in the left navigation) has two tabs, analytics and automations; there is no members table and no invitation for members (finding N-02). The only invitation dialog is 'Invite a client' for guests.
sources: The prototype has no sign-in screen for members, only the guest one. How do members sign in, and how are accounts created? (D-011)
You chose the recommended option: (b) 6-digit emailed code, no password, admin invitation only, 30-day session
A fresh installation has no accounts. How does the first Owner come to exist? (D-028)
Your answer: Created from environment variables or seed; that admin invites members
The prototype shows Owner, Admin and ordinary members but no difference between them. Who is allowed to do what? (D-012)
You chose the recommended option: As in the capability table under Roles & States
How long does an invitation last, and does its link need a sign-in code? (D-037)
You confirmed: An invitation expires after 7 days. The link in the invitation signs the person in directly, without a code.
**Assumed, not confirmed (D-134):** Batches of invitations are limited to 50 addresses.

charts.title: 2.13 Admin: change a role, deactivate a member
notes: **Before:** signed in as Admin or Owner, on the Admin page.
**Who may do what:** only an Owner changes roles. An Admin deactivates Members; only an Owner deactivates Admins and Owners.
**Constraints:** nobody deactivates themselves; the last Owner cannot be demoted or deactivated.
**After (role):** the label updates on Admin, People and the profile; the person gets an Activity item and sees the Admin entry appear or disappear.

**After (deactivate):** every session ends; old messages stay with a 'Deactivated' label; the person leaves People, mention lists and add-people lists; DMs with them become read-only. Reactivate restores access to the same channels.
**Cancel:** closing the confirmation changes nothing.
**In the prototype:** **Not in the prototype.** Admin has no members table, so there is no role menu and no Deactivate (finding N-02). People and the profile panel show a role label, read-only.
sources: The prototype shows Owner, Admin and ordinary members but no difference between them. Who is allowed to do what? (D-012)
You chose the recommended option: As in the capability table under Roles & States
Can there be several Owners, and what protects the last one? (D-039)
You confirmed: There can be several Owners. The last Owner cannot be demoted or deactivated.

**Rule D-069** (made from GAP-24 · D-061): A reversible action happens at once and shows a toast with Undo for 5 seconds. An irreversible action, or one that affects other people, asks for confirmation and names its target. Never both for one action.

charts.title: 2.14 Start a direct message or a group
notes: **Before:** signed in as Member, Admin or Owner. Guests cannot start DMs.
**After:** the conversation is open. The other people see it in their list only once the first message is sent.
**Limit:** a group holds at most 8 people, counting the person who starts it. Nobody can be added or removed later; a different set of people is a new group.
**Same people, same conversation:** choosing a set of people that already has a conversation reopens it with its history.
**Deactivated person:** not listed in the picker; an existing DM with them stays readable, without a composer.

**In the prototype:** 'New message' is the pencil icon above the conversation list. Its dialog has one field, 'Search people and channels'; pressing a row opens that DM or channel at once. **Several people cannot be chosen**, so a group cannot be started. One group exists as sample data only: 'Alex, Thu', three people.
sources: Which message features are in phase 1 and which wait? And what about three things the prototype does not have: @channel, a full emoji picker, and group DMs with several people? (D-017)

Can people be added to or removed from a group DM? (D-045)
You confirmed: People cannot be added to or removed from a group DM.
The prototype shows Owner, Admin and ordinary members but no difference between them. Who is allowed to do what? (D-012)
You chose the recommended option: As in the capability table under Roles & States

charts.title: 3.1 The connection drops and returns
notes: **Rule:** loaded content stays readable; messages being sent wait and send themselves; every other action is blocked with an explanation, never a false success.
**Catch-up:** the app remembers the number of the last event it saw and asks for everything after it. After more than 7 days away it reloads everything instead.
**No duplicates:** a waiting message is resent with its original ID.
**Banner:** it never covers the composer or the navigation.

**In the prototype:** A demo switch turns the network off. The prototype then shows a strip above the chat, 'Offline: showing saved messages · messages you send wait until you are back online', the same words above the conversation list, and 'Waiting to send' on messages. **'Reconnecting…' and 'Reconnected' are not in the prototype**, and other actions are not blocked (GAP-21).
sources: **Rule D-079** (made from GAP-21 · D-060): When the connection drops: loaded content stays readable; messages being sent wait and send themselves when the connection returns; every other action is blocked with an explanation, never a false success.
**Rule D-078** (made from GAP-03, 11): Toasts and floating bars never cover the composer or navigation.
**Technical design:** Every change is a numbered event. After reconnecting, the app asks for everything after the last number it saw; after more than 7 days away it reloads.
**Assumed, not confirmed (D-129):** Reconnect attempts wait 1, 2, 5, 10 and then 30 seconds, with a little randomness.
**Assumed, not confirmed (D-132):** A 'Waiting to send' message survives a page reload, kept in the browser, and is dropped if someone else signs in on that browser.
**Assumed, not confirmed (D-140):** While offline the banner keeps the prototype's words, 'Offline: showing saved messages'. A separate 'Reconnecting…' state is not assumed.

charts.title: 3.2 The session ends while the app is in use
notes: **Before:** the app is open with a session that has just stopped being valid.
**After:** nothing of the workspace stays readable on screen; after signing in again the person is back in the same conversation with the draft still in the composer.
**Rule:** the server checks the session on every request and closes the realtime connection the moment a session ends.
**Rule:** a deactivated account gets no sign-in button, and its locally kept drafts are cleared.
**In the prototype:** **Not in the prototype.** It has no sign-in and no sessions, so none of these screens exist (finding N-01).
sources: The prototype has no sign-in screen for members, only the guest one. How do members sign in, and how are accounts created? (D-011)
You chose the recommended option: (b) 6-digit emailed code, no password, admin invitation only, 30-day session
The prototype shows Owner, Admin and ordinary members but no difference between them. Who is allowed to do what? (D-012)
You chose the recommended option: As in the capability table under Roles & States
**Technical design:** The server checks the session on every request and closes the live connection the moment a session ends.
**Assumed, not confirmed (D-132):** A 'Waiting to send' message survives a page reload, kept in the browser, and is dropped if someone else signs in on that browser.

**Assumed, not confirmed (D-139):** Every screen and every wording in quotes that the prototype does not contain is a proposal: 'Session ended', 'Account deactivated', 'Not found or no access', 'Not sent', 'Can't reach Toki', loading placeholders, and the rest.

charts.title: 3.3 A request is refused or fails: one behaviour for every feature
notes: **Disabled while waiting:** the control that started the request is disabled and shows a spinner, so nothing is submitted twice.
**Form kept:** a refusal never clears what the person typed.
**No access and not found look the same**, so the app never confirms that a private thing exists.
**Error ID:** a server error shows a short ID the person can pass on; the same ID is in the server log.
**401** is handled by flow 3.2 for every request.

**In the prototype:** **Not in the prototype.** There is no server; every action succeeds at once. The words 'error' and 'Retry' do not occur in it (finding N-06). Problems in forms are reported by a toast after pressing the button (finding N-08).
sources: **Rule D-070** (made from GAP-22 · D-061): A form that has content does not close on an outside click; closing it by button asks whether to discard.
**Assumed, not confirmed (D-126):** A request with no answer after 10 seconds counts as failed and shows Retry.
**Assumed, not confirmed (D-131):** Server status codes map to screens as in flow 3.3: 400 field message, 403 and 404 one shared page, 409 and 410 fresh copy, 429 wait, 5xx Retry with an error ID.

**Assumed, not confirmed (D-139):** Every screen and every wording in quotes that the prototype does not contain is a proposal: 'Session ended', 'Account deactivated', 'Not found or no access', 'Not sent', 'Can't reach Toki', loading placeholders, and the rest.
